expectations.text: States it is not insurance advice and that whether any policy responds to a specific loss is a question for the broker reading the actual wording.
expectations.evidence: "not insurance or legal advice. The broker decides which policy fits and whether it responds to a given loss."

expectations.text: Recommends asking explicitly whether the cancellation form includes a communicable-disease buy-back, and what it costs.
expectations.evidence: "Communicable-disease buy-back, priced as its own line. If it is not available, please say so in writing."

expectations.text: States that insurers excluded the communicable-disease peril market-wide from late January 2020, and that it has been available since only as a specifically negotiated endorsement.
expectations.evidence: Says only "Insurers excluded that peril market-wide from early 2020". It doesn't say late January or that it is available only as a negotiated endorsement.

expectations.text: Instructs recording the disease buy-back decision either way, with its reason, including when it is declined.
expectations.evidence: "We will record the decision either way"; "Record the disease buy-back decision with its reason."

expectations.text: Promotes parametric or adverse-weather cover because part of the event is outdoors, rather than leaving it at the bottom of the ladder.
expectations.evidence: "Half the day is in a marquee on a lawn, so weather cover is promoted."

expectations.text: For any parametric structure, says to ask which station measures the index, over which hours, and what the trigger would have paid in prior years.
expectations.evidence: "key hours set to the event day. The nearest measuring station. What the trigger would have paid in each of the last five years".

expectations.text: Warns that a trigger that never fires in a bad year is worse than no cover, because it was still paid for.
expectations.evidence: No such warning appears.

expectations.text: Recommends participant accident cover and ties it to the hands-on hardware (soldering bench, drone cage) rather than offering it generically.

expectations.text: States that general liability frequently does not pay attendee medical expenses, which is why participant accident cover complements rather than duplicates it.
expectations.evidence: It only asks "say whether the liability policy pays attendee medical expenses". It makes no statement.
